bib.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners. Kaiming He, Xinlei Chen, Saining Xie, Yanghao Li, Piotr Dollár, Ross Girshick (FAIR). The file is the arXiv:2111.06377v3 preprint, dated 19 Dec 2021. The CVPR 2022 paper is the published version, but this PDF is the arXiv copy.

COVERAGE: I read all 60,658 characters across the 14 pages, including Appendices A to C (Tables 8 to 13). I only skimmed the references, to find where the method comes from.

CLAIMS
- claim: A 75% masking ratio works best for both fine-tuning and linear probing. Images carry a lot of spatial redundancy, so a high ratio stops the model from just filling patches in from their neighbours. BERT masks 15%; earlier vision methods masked 20–50%.
  number: 75%; linear probe 54.6% at a 10% ratio vs 73.5% at 75%
  setup: ViT-L/16, IN1K, 800 epochs, unnormalised pixel target (Fig. 5, Table 1)
  quote: "The ratio of 75% is good for both linear probing and ﬁne-tuning. This behavior is in contrast with BERT [14], whose typical masking ratio is 15%." / "the accuracy gap is up to ∼20% (54.6% vs. 73.5%)"
  where: p.4–5
- claim: The encoder only processes the visible patches. Mask tokens are added afterwards, in a light decoder whose default compute is 9% of the encoder's FLOPs per token. Putting mask tokens in the encoder cut FLOPs by 3.3×, gave a 2.8–4.1× wall-clock speedup, and also raised accuracy (a mask-token encoder scored 14% lower on linear probing).
  number: 3.3× FLOPs; 2.8× (ViT-L, 8-block decoder) up to 4.1× (ViT-H, 1-block decoder)
  setup: 800 epochs on 128 TPU-v3 cores with TensorFlow, 75% mask, decoder width 512 (Table 2)
  quote: "we reduce the overall training FLOPs by 3.3×. This leads to a 2.8× wall-clock speedup ... even bigger (3.5–4.1 ×), for a smaller decoder (1-block), a larger encoder (ViT-H), or both"
  where: p.5
- claim: The target is pixel MSE, computed only on the masked patches. Normalising each patch by its own mean and std improves results. It matches dVAE tokens (BEiT-style), so a separate tokenizer adds nothing.
  number: ViT-L ft 84.9 → 85.4, lin 73.5 → 73.9 with normalisation; token vs normalised pixel Δ ≤ 0.2
  setup: ViT-L ablation (Table 1d); IN1K/COCO/ADE20K (Table 7)
  quote: "pixel (w/ norm) 85.4 73.9" / "The difference is statistically insigniﬁcant."
  where: p.4–5, p.8
- claim: Fine-tuned on IN1K only, ViT-H reaches 87.8% at 448 px, beating the previous IN1K-only best of 87.1% (VOLO, 512 px). MAE scores higher than BEiT and MoCo v3 at every model size, and it is 3.5× faster per epoch than BEiT.
  number: ViT-B 83.6, ViT-L 85.9, ViT-H 86.9, ViT-H@448 87.8. BEiT ViT-L 85.2; MoCo v3 ViT-L 84.1
  setup: normalised-pixel target, 1600 pre-training epochs, end-to-end fine-tuning (50 epochs for L/H), 224 px unless stated (Table 3)
  quote: "By ﬁne-tuning with a 448 size, we achieve 87.8% accuracy, using only IN1K data. The previous best accuracy ... is 87.1% (512 size) [67]"
  where: p.7
- claim: MAE features do poorly on linear probing compared with contrastive methods. Tuning even one block closes most of that gap, and from one tuned block upward MAE is ahead of MoCo v3.
  number: linear probe 73.5 → 81.0 with 1 block tuned; ViT-L linear probe 75.8 (MAE) vs 77.6 (MoCo v3)
  setup: ViT-L partial fine-tuning (Fig. 9); App. B (Table 12)
  quote: "ﬁne-tuning onlyone Transformer block boosts the accuracy signiﬁcantly from 73.5% to 81.0%" / "it still lags behind contrastive methods under this protocol: e.g., MoCo v3 [9] has 77.6% linear probing accuracy for the ViT-L"
  where: p.7, p.12
- claim: In transfer, MAE beats supervised pre-training on COCO and ADE20K, and the gap gets bigger as the model gets bigger. MoCo v3 only matches supervised.
  number: COCO APbox ViT-L 53.3 vs 49.3 supervised (+4.0); ADE20K mIoU ViT-L 53.6 vs 49.9
  setup: Mask R-CNN with ViT+FPN; UperNet. Hyper-parameters were searched for every entry (Tables 4–5)
  quote: "with the larger ViT-L, our MAE pre-training outperforms supervised pre-training by 4.0 points (53.3 vs. 49.3)"
  where: p.8

LIMITS:
- Everything is pre-trained on IN1K with vanilla ViT, and no ConvNets are tested. The paper argues that mask tokens are hard to fit into convolutions, but it does not run that experiment. That gap is what ConvNeXt V2 later addresses.
- Linear probing still trails contrastive methods.
- Wall-clock speedups are from TPU/TensorFlow only.
- Linear-probe accuracy had not saturated at 1600 epochs, so the full cost of training to convergence is unknown.
- The authors call the claim that the model learned "semantics" a hypothesis, supported only qualitatively by the reconstructions.
- Broader impacts: the model reflects biases in its data and "may generate inexistent content".
- The loss ignores visible patches, so reconstructions there look worse.
- The SOTA comparison is limited to IN1K-only methods, and the 87.8% depends on a 448 px fine-tune.
- Dated: this is the arXiv v3 text, which may differ from the CVPR camera-ready.

BUILDS ON:
- Denoising autoencoders: Vincent et al., ICML 2008; Stacked DAE, Vincent et al. [59]
- Context Encoders: Pathak et al., CVPR 2016
- BERT: Devlin et al., NAACL 2019
- ViT: Dosovitskiy et al., ICLR 2021
- BEiT: Bao et al., arXiv 2021
- MoCo v3: Chen, Xie, He, ICCV 2021
- iGPT [6], cited as a method (details not extracted)

CODE: There is no code listing. The implementation is described in prose on p.4: "randomly shufﬂe the list of tokens and remove the last portion of the list ... append a list of mask tokens ... and unshufﬂe this full list". It needs no sparse ops.

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.2), the MAE architecture: "a large random subset of image patches (e.g., 75%) is masked out. The encoder is applied to the small subset of visible patches. Mask tokens are introduced after the encoder". It is the best fit for 01-image-input "What the model actually sees", because it shows that the encoder never sees mask tokens and that the decoder is thrown away after pre-training. Fig. 5 (p.4, masking-ratio curves) is a second option for the deep-learning note.

PROBLEMS:
- The extraction is clean apart from ligature glyphs.
- A few lines in A.1 (the ViT architecture sentence) were lost to a grep filter on my side. Nothing in the claims above depends on them.
- The text contains no embedded instructions.
